title: Freddie Newman and the Silver Slipper club
summary: Freddie Newman was his piano player at the Ringside, and he recalls the Italian-owned nightclub on Bienville Street.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Well when I was with Detroit, Freddie Newman was playing. Freddie Newman was the piano player with Detroit when I played with Detroit. Freddie Newman, yeah. Yeah, you played with Freddie Newman at the Bienville Roof, didn't you? Yeah.

Oh, I played with Freddie Newman plenty of times. I played with Freddie Newman. Freddie Newman was our piano player when we played at the ringside for Pete Whippen. And then when we played for, what is his name, I can't think of his name, he had a nightclub on Bienville Street.
Oh, hell, what is his name? Musician-only club?
Near the fern, around in that area? Is that the district or down here?

No, no, right here on Bienville Street between, I believe it was between Boybin and Dolphine, or both. No, the Dolphine, Bienville between Dolphine and Bergogne. It used to be a dying dancing hall. And this fella picked it up and made a nightclub on him. Trambina! Trambina. That's his name. That's Trambina. I'm coming around. He had a dress, then he opened, he closed that. Which is right now, what they call it, the forest cafe or whatever.
Oh yeah, I found it with Mustangs.
Yeah, well it was named the Silver Slipper.
Oh sure, that was the name of what I can't remember.
Well, I went to work then. Yeah.
